newsitem.title: USA: Apple operations chief Scalise to resign, join SIA.
newsitem.headline: Apple operations chief Scalise to resign, join SIA.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc. said Tuesday that Chief Operating Officer George Scalise will resign after a little more than a year on the job, extending the list of top executives who have left the troubled computer maker in the past year to half a dozen.
Scalise, who was responsible for managing Apple's manufacturing operations, said he will become the president of the Semiconductor Industry Association, the chip industry's chief trade group.

"The main reason I'm leaving is that I had some objectives when I came here," including figuring out how to manage Apple's assets better, to get product development going again and to restructure the business, Scalise said. "That has been largely accomplished."
Apple will eliminate his position, he said.
Scalise was one of the several executives who joined Apple shortly after Gilbert Amelio became Apple Chairman in February 1996.
Many of those new executives and several Apple veterans have quit in the past year, however, as Apple struggled through two restructurings in 13 months.
Scalise said Amelio will take over some of his duties temporarily. Other Apple executives will absorb his duties.
Scalise's departure is the biggest since Marco Landi, executive vice president, left in February. Shortly before that, Heidi Roizen, the company's liaison to software developers, left.
